To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the NIH Clinical Collection was screened to identify clinically approved drugs that enhance transfection by PEI, which may be useful to increase transgene expression and reduce the dose of nonviral gene delivery vectors in clinical applications.

a high‐throughout screen was performed of 1,040 clinical compounds to identify clinical compounds which prime PEI transfection, and that compounds identified in the screen are clustered by drug class and associated with mitochondria function.
the NCC was screened to identify transfection priming clinical compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of compounds that enhance nonviral transfection efficiency.
the identification of compounds that prime transfection by PEI.
the identification of transfection primers that increase gene transfer efficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NCC library screen identified compounds that prime transfection of PEI, which can be used in future studies for the development of new tools to enhance transfection efficiency.
a high‐throughputs screen was performed of clinical drug compounds, and compounds that prime transfection by polyethylenemine were identified.
a high‐throughputscreening of the NCC identified several classes of compounds that prime PEI transfection, and that these compounds may act by modulating the mitochondrial response to transfection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the identified transfection‐priming drug classes, such as antioxidants and glucocorticoid, may be used to enhance gene delivery and transgene expression by nonviral methods.
we have developed a high‐through put screening method to identify transfection‐priming compounds, which may be used to develop new tools to improve gene delivery efficiency.
the NCC screen identified compounds from drug classes that prime polyethyleneimine transfection, and that modulation of mitochondria may be a mechanism for transfection priming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high‐throughput screening approach we used to screen the NCC for transfection priming drugs can be used for other drug libraries and transfection methods.
the high‐throughput screening method can identify transfection priming drugs, and the identified transfection‐priming drug classes may be used to design novel transfection‐enhancing agents.
a high‐throughputs screen can be used to identify compounds that prime nonviral transfection, and that these compounds may be used to improve nonviral transgene delivery.
